sources.title: Anthropic Fermat Lean formalization science article (11 days, 13M lines)
sources.role: Discovery-bounded source used for factual verification

claims.text: Anthropic dated Sep 4 reports the first complete computer-checked Fermat proof in Lean: ~11 days largely autonomous, 13M Lean lines, 29,500 theorems used in the final proof (30,300 proved), following a simplified Darmon-Diamond-Taylor version of Wiles.
claims.context: Vendor research article; scale figures vendor-reported.

claims.text: Dozens of Claude agents via a Claude Code harness on the Prove2Me platform (theorem DAG, split statement/proof compilation, natural-language search/reuse) consumed ~6B output tokens from a general internal model roughly comparable to Claude Fable 5.1; human input was limited to high-level prompts, with ~7% of non-boilerplate lines from failed early attempts.
claims.context: Vendor process account; model identity is approximate.

claims.text: The finished proof was checked by Lean using only its 3 standard axioms, and a comparator confirmed the statement matches Mathlib's own FLT statement.
claims.context: Verification facts as stated; Lean/comparator rerun is not performed by this record.

claims.text: Reviewer Kevin Buzzard is quoted calling it an extraordinary autoformalization achievement proving FLT on mathematics axioms alone with robust multi-layered artefacts, supporting automatic formalization of the literature and referee-load reduction.
claims.context: Reviewer quote as published on the vendor page; independent reverification separate.
